I would keep this year simple and steady. I am 63, and I do not want to gamble on crops that need complicated management or heavy daily labor. In Quzhou County, the crop I trust most is the usual wheat and maize rotation. I know this land, I know this weather pattern, and I know how to manage these two crops with the tools and experience I already have. That matters more to me than chasing a crop with a higher price but more risk.

So on my main land, I would stay with winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same fields. I would use improved or hybrid seed, because I want stable emergence, better disease resistance, and more dependable yield. I would not plant many scattered small crops, because that makes field work, fertilizer use, irrigation, and spraying harder to manage. I would prepare the land with rotary tillage because it is easier for me than deep ploughing every time, and it matches the way I would handle residue and sowing.

For fertilizer, I would not go too light because that would hold back yield, but I would also not push too hard because fertilizer is expensive and too much nitrogen can bring lodging and waste. For wheat, I would give enough water at the key stages, especially wintering, jointing, and grain filling if water is available. For maize, I would focus irrigation around the big demand periods after establishment and around tasseling to grain filling. I would spray only when needed for the common weeds, insects, and diseases I usually see, because I want to control damage without adding unnecessary cost.
